summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at National Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Pakistan posted 191/10 (59.3 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Sri Lanka countered with 271/10 (85.5 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: Abid Ali 174 (283b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Abid Ali delivered a masterclass for Pakistan (212 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Pakistan 69%) and allowing Pakistan to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Sri Lanka faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Pakistan's bowling unit, bolstered by Babar Azam (160 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Pakistan won by 263 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Pakistan's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Sri Lanka produced fighting phases, Pakistan won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
